ai.description: This tiny toad reaches 20–25 mm. It is brown with a dark, X-shaped dorsal pattern and a pale mid-dorsal stripe. It lacks a tympanum and possesses a distinct, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Andaman Bush Toad is best distinguished by its extremely small size (under 25mm) and the presence of a distinct, dark, X-shaped marking on its dorsal surface.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Bush Toad inhabits the leaf litter of primary and secondary tropical evergreen forests in the Andaman Islands, typically at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Bush Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its forest floor habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: Blythophryne beryet exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in moist forest leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Andaman Bush Toad is endemic to the Andaman Islands, India, where it inhabits lowland tropical forests at elevations ranging from near sea level to 300 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Andaman Bush Toad emits a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of a rapid series of pulsed notes, typically heard from leaf litter in moist tropical forests.
